critical_code_review_comments: Pips() cleanly derives box = fs*1.3 and centers the Text inside — good buffer against font ascent/descent asymmetry on native, which was the root cause of the reported drift.
The 180° rotation is applied on the wrapper View (not on the Text), which is the correct place for RN — layout coordinates are computed before the transform, so rotated pips stay pixel-anchored.
Ace wrapper uses left/right/top/bottom = 0 with centered flex — deterministic on both native and web; no reliance on lineHeight quirks.
CourtCenter's in-frame suit pips are also View-wrapped now; symmetry preserved with the number-card pip approach.

To re-verify: (a) grep -n "position" /app/frontend/src/components/PlayingCard.tsx should show 7 hits, all on Views (never on Text). (c) Native check requires an EAS build — not reproducible headless; web verification here plus the structural guarantee is the accepted pass path.
rca_of_issue: Root cause (per bug report, confirmed by code diff): on native RN, a <Text> element carrying its own position:'absolute' style is measured after font-layout — the resulting box drifts because RN's Yoga positions the text baseline, not the visual glyph center, and stacks siblings with the same left origin. Absolute-positioned Views are laid out by Yoga BEFORE their text children measure, so a View→Text nesting produces stable coordinates identical to what web already shows. Fix applied by main agent wraps each pip glyph in an absolute View with fixed width/height and flex-centered Text (includeFontPadding:false, allowFontScaling:false to remove OS-dependent padding). Verified: 8 pip Views on 8♠ render at exactly [(0.31,0.18),(0.69,0.18),(0.5,0.33),(0.31,0.5),(0.69,0.5),(0.5,0.67),(0.31,0.82),(0.69,0.82)] of card width/height, with bottom halves rotated 180°.
